references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, the holy anointing oil and its composition are described, which this verse refers to.
Aaron is anointed with the holy oil, illustrating the use of the anointing oil in priestly consecration.
Moses receives a command to anoint Aaron's sons, and the anointing is to give them an eternal priesthood through their generations.
Moses pours the anointing oil on Aaron's head to consecrate him, fulfilling the command regarding the holy oil.
The high priest who is anointed with the holy oil is mentioned, showing the lasting significance of the oil.
God anoints David with His holy oil, linking the anointing oil to the kingdom and the Messianic promises.
The precious oil that runs down over Aaron's head and beard describes the holiness and blessing of the anointing oil.
Christ is anointed with the oil of gladness above His companions, fulfilling the Old Testament picture of holy anointing.
The anointing as a sanctifying means (30:31) is the ritual basis for the call to become a royal priesthood and a holy nation (19:6).
Both the anointing and the Sabbath serve as eternal signs that the Lord is the one who sanctifies His people through all generations.
The anointing (30:31) is a concrete expression of the general call to be holy because God is holy (19:2).
The eternal holy status of the anointing (30:31) is supported by the warning against those who profane the holy gifts (22:3).
